# TAO (JUNO-TAO), arXiv:2610.23331v1, Fig. 25b: predicted energy non-linearity E_rec/E_true for e+, e- and gamma
# with their 68% C.L. uncertainty bands. Extracted from the vector graphics in the PDF (page 29); axis calibration
# from the tick marks (x: 0-12 MeV true energy; y: 0.80-1.10).
#
# Columns: E_true_MeV, then for each particle: nominal (solid line), lo/hi (edges of the shaded band).
#  positron: true energy = T_e+ + 1.022 MeV, so the curve starts at 1.022 MeV (2 m_e); 'nan' below that.
#            The curve ends at 11.992 MeV in the PDF, so 12.00 MeV is 'nan'.
#  electron, gamma: start at 0.01-0.02 MeV. Values below 0.80 lie outside the visible plot frame (clipped in
#            the figure) but are present in the PDF paths and are reported as stored.
#
# Precision:
#  - Bands: stored as polygons with 1098-1200 points per edge (one every ~0.01 MeV), so they are exact.
#  - Nominal lines: stored as 42 (e+), 47 (e-) and 181 (gamma) vertices; linear interpolation between them is
#    good to ~5e-4 (e+, e-). The e+ and e- lines sit at the band centre to within 3e-4 and 6e-4.
#  - The gamma line lies up to 0.0025 off the band centre; with 181 vertices this is a real asymmetry of the band,
#    not an interpolation artefact.
# Note from the paper: the fit uncertainty on the e+ curve is quoted as about 1% at high energy, and it was
# enlarged to 2% at high energy in the reactor analysis. The e+ band drawn here reaches a half-width of ~1.75%
# at 10 MeV and ~2% near 12 MeV, so the plotted band may already include that enlargement; the paper does not
# say which version is shown.
#
